question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and what default plus hook-extra semantics should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/22439 use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a public config/default surface affects prompt context, session behavior, upgrade expectations, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the linked PR shape
options.body: Proceed with maintainer review of the linked PR as the focused additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this item behind broader deterministic bootstrap/context selection work and design one public selector contract covering tiering, per-session filtering, and related prompt-pressure work together.

options.title: Decline a new config knob
options.body: Keep fixed filters and steer users toward existing contextInjection, per-agent bootstrap budgets, lightweight mode, or doctor guidance instead of adding bootstrapTier.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the linked PR shape
recommendation.body: Proceed with maintainer review of the linked PR as the focused additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.
